CA_STEPS|/planA/points/3: for drinking water structures: {CL170}, {CP360} and {CP350} are tested after DVGW W 270 and W 347
CA_STEPS|/planA/points/4: the construction joints are planned with the system accessories: {CJ5}, {CJ6}, {CJ1}
CA_STEPS|/testA/short: The functionality of the recipe including the admixture is verified in an initial test; the dosing level follows the w/c ratio and the cement content.
CA_STEPS|/testA/overview: The functionality of the concrete mix design including BETOCRETE is verified as part of an initial test; preliminary tests must always be carried out — also when other admixtures are combined with it. The dosing level of the data sheet follows the w/c ratio: liquid 1.75 % (< 0.4), 1.85 % (> 0.4–0.5), 2.00 % (> 0.5–0.55) of the cement weight, never above 2.25 %; powder 0.75 / 0.80 / 0.90 % ({CP360}) or 0.75 / 0.80 / 0.95 % ({CP350}), never above 1.25 %. For a cement content of ≥ 400 kg/m³ 7.00 kg/m³ (liquid) or 3.50 kg/m³ (powder) is sufficient.
CA_STEPS|/testA/points/0: the dosage depends on the cement content and the w/c ratio of the recipe; the table serves as a guide
CA_STEPS|/testA/points/1: in rare cases the admixture can influence the solidification behaviour of the concrete: the system-compatible retarder {RUX} is available for controlling the concrete
CA_STEPS|/testA/points/2: {CL170}: water saving up to 10 % — the water content of the recipe is adjusted in the initial test
CA_STEPS|/testA/points/3: the quantity of a liquid admixture is deducted from the mixing water
CA_STEPS|/doseP/title: Dose the liquid admixture in the plant
CA_STEPS|/doseP/short: BETOCRETE-CL dosed with the mixing water or into the finished mix by the dosing system of the plant; mixed for more than 45 seconds; deducted from the mixing water.
CA_STEPS|/doseP/overview: Liquid BETOCRETE is dosed directly into the concrete mix via the dosing system of the concrete plant — with the mixing water or into the finished concrete mixture — without additional work steps and precisely, with automated pump technology. The mixing time in the concrete plant is more than 45 seconds. The quantity of the admixture is deducted from the mixing water.
CA_STEPS|/doseP/points/0: dosing approx. 1.75–2.25 % of the cement weight; never above 2.25 %
CA_STEPS|/doseP/points/1: application temperature approx. 8–40 °C; stir the admixture after storage of more than one month
CA_STEPS|/doseP/points/2: colour change of the admixture above +30 °C is harmless
CA_STEPS|/doseP/points/3: IBC (1,100 kg {CL170} / 1,040 kg {CL210}), 220 kg drums and 25 kg cans; storage frost-free at 8–40 °C
CA_STEPS|/doseC/title: Dose the powder admixture in the plant
CA_STEPS|/doseC/short: BETOCRETE-CP dosed onto the aggregates and mixed for at least 30 seconds before water and cement are added; then mixed for at least 45 seconds.
CA_STEPS|/doseC/overview: {CP360} and {CP350} must be dosed onto the aggregates and mixed for at least 30 seconds before adding the water and the cement. Then the mixing is finished for at least 45 seconds until the concrete is ready for use. The powder is supplied in watertight foil bags (17 kg {CP360}, 20 kg {CP350}) for metering into the mixer.
CA_STEPS|/doseC/points/0: dosing approx. 0.75–1.25 % of the cement weight; never above 1.25 %
CA_STEPS|/doseC/points/2: for a cement content of ≥ 400 kg/m³ a dosing level of 3.50 kg/m³ is sufficient
CA_STEPS|/doseC/points/3: storage cool, dry and protected from sunlight, min. 24 months; opened containers are used promptly
CA_STEPS|/truckA/title: Dose into the mixer truck on site
CA_STEPS|/truckA/short: Powder as 3 kg water-soluble bags, liquid poured into the drum; approx. 1 minute of mixing per m³ of drum content, at least 5 minutes.
CA_STEPS|/truckA/overview: Where the admixture is added on site, the powder goes into the drum of the mixer truck as 3 kg water-soluble bags and liquid BETOCRETE-CL is poured directly into the mixing drum. The mixing time is approx. 1 minute per m³ of drum content, but at least 5 minutes. For the liquid the quantity is deducted from the mixing water.
CA_STEPS|/truckA/points/0: water-soluble bags of {CP360} and {CP350}: 192 per pallet, also as a cardboard version ({CP360})
CA_STEPS|/truckA/points/1: water-soluble paper bags may increase the water demand ({CP360})
CA_STEPS|/truckA/points/2: the number of bags per load follows from the cement content of the load and the dosing level
CA_STEPS|/truckA/points/3: the mixing time is counted after the last bag has gone in
CA_STEPS|/jointA/short: The crystalline waterstop AQUAFIN-CJ5 in the kicker; the swelling tape AQUAFIN-CJ6 on working joints; the injection hose AQUAFIN-CJ1 as reserve.
CA_STEPS|/jointA/overview: The construction joint is the classic weak point in waterproofing. The system accessories for the construction joint provide the solution: in addition to grouting and expanding waterstops, the crystalline construction metal waterstop {CJ5} offers a high level of safety. It extends the circulation of the water on the possible path through the cracked joint; its cementitious coating forms a high adhesion bond with the concrete, so that the probability of cracking is reduced; the metal waterstop is ready to use and not prone to processing errors — no film has to be peeled off; if there is a crack in the construction joint, crystal formation is induced by the metal waterstop and the cracks are sealed.
CA_STEPS|/jointA/points/0: {CJ5} is fixed to the reinforcement in the kicker before the wall is poured and cast in by the wall
CA_STEPS|/jointA/points/1: working joints: the swelling joint tape {CJ6} on the hardened concrete
CA_STEPS|/jointA/points/2: critical joints: the injection hose {CJ1} as reserve, injected only if the joint leaks
CA_STEPS|/jointA/points/3: movement joints are not construction joints: they are formed with the joint tapes of the ASO-Dichtband system †
CA_STEPS|/placeA/title: Place, compact and finish the concrete
CA_STEPS|/placeA/short: As watertight concrete to the valid standards: full compaction, no segregation, no added water on site; the admixture does not replace the craft.
CA_STEPS|/placeA/overview: Concrete with BETOCRETE must be produced, applied and post-treated in accordance with the currently valid standards. The admixture changes neither the placing nor the compaction: the concrete is placed in layers, fully compacted, and no water is added on site †. The crystalline effect works in a dense concrete — honeycombs and voids are not sealed by crystals but repaired.
CA_STEPS|/placeA/points/0: no additional water on site: it raises the w/c ratio beyond the recipe †
CA_STEPS|/placeA/points/1: fully compacted, placed in layers without cold joints †
CA_STEPS|/placeA/points/2: {CL170} gives a smoother consistency at a lower water content; the water saving is part of the recipe, not an allowance on site
CA_STEPS|/placeA/points/3: honeycombs and voids are broken out and repaired with the ASOCRET-BIS system before the component is loaded †
CA_STEPS|/cureA/short: Kept damp and protected to the valid standards; crystals may appear on the surface, depending on the composition — not a defect.
CA_STEPS|/cureA/overview: The curing of the concrete follows the currently valid standards for watertight concrete: the surfaces are protected against drying out, wind, sun and frost and kept damp †. BETOCRETE-modified concretes may show crystals on the surface, depending on the composition; the colour and the moisture content of the concrete have no bearing on the function.
CA_STEPS|/cureA/points/0: curing to the standards: the crystalline effect needs the dense concrete the curing produces †
CA_STEPS|/cureA/points/1: crystals on the surface are not a defect
CA_STEPS|/cureA/points/2: the formwork is struck when the strength allows †
CA_STEPS|/cureA/points/3: the surfaces are not coated before they have been assessed: cracks wider than 0.4 mm and moving cracks are injected
CA_STEPS|/crackA/short: Crack-width limits by the planner and engineer; cracks up to 0.4 mm heal themselves; wider or moving cracks are injected.
CA_STEPS|/crackA/overview: The crack expansion limitations must be complied with by the planner, engineer and structural engineer under any circumstances; contrary designs are verified after the corresponding verification and suitability. Surface and continuous cracks up to 0.4 mm (tapering down to 0.5 mm) heal themselves by crystal growth when water reaches them. Movements in the concrete component — traffic loads, temperature differences — can cause sealed crystalline cracks to open again; they heal again when water arrives.
CA_STEPS|/crackA/points/0: crack injections for non-dynamic separating cracks up to 0.4 mm can often be omitted due to the crack-healing ability
CA_STEPS|/crackA/points/1: cracks wider than 0.4 mm and dynamic cracks are injected: {P1}, {P4}, {IH}
CA_STEPS|/crackA/points/2: the injection hose {CJ1} in a critical joint is the reserve
CA_STEPS|/serviceA/short: The ground water presses, the pores close, the inside stays dry; the reserve of active ingredient stays in the matrix for life.
CA_STEPS|/serviceA/overview: When the water load arrives the active ingredient dissolves in the pore water, reacts with the calcium hydroxide of the hydration and grows insoluble crystals in the capillary pores: the capillary zone shifts outwards, the reinforcement lies in the dry core, moisture leaves the inside face as vapour only. The more compact pore structure reduces the chloride ion migration and the carbonation rate and improves the frost and freeze–thaw resistance. The reserve of unreacted active ingredient remains in the matrix for the life of the component.
CA_STEPS|/serviceA/points/0: the sealant of {CL210} and {CP360} has been reducing the water absorption by more than half from the first day
CA_STEPS|/serviceA/points/1: water-retaining structures: {CL170}, {CP360} and {CP350} are tested for drinking water
CA_STEPS|/serviceA/points/2: the component is as watertight as the concrete is sound: the recipe, the compaction and the joints decide
CA_STEPS|/notesA/title: Observe the limits of the data sheets
CA_STEPS|/notesA/short: No XA3, no CEM III/C; preliminary tests; the retarder RUXOLITH-T5 where the setting is affected; safety data sheets.
CA_STEPS|/notesA/overview: The data sheets set the limits: concretes of exposure class XA3 are excluded; CEM III/C cements are prohibited (CEM III/B also for {CL170}, {CL210} and {CP350}); lignite fly ash is of limited suitability; the crack expansion limitations are complied with. In rare cases the admixture can influence the solidification behaviour of the concrete — the system-compatible retarder {RUX} is available for controlling the concrete. Preliminary tests must always be carried out.
CA_STEPS|/notesA/points/0: observe the applicable safety data sheets
CA_STEPS|/notesA/points/1: liquids: stir after storage of more than one month; store frost-free at 8–40 °C; a colour change above +30 °C is harmless
CA_STEPS|/notesA/points/2: powders: store cool, dry and protected from sunlight for min. 24 months; use opened containers promptly
CA_STEPS|/notesA/points/3: as the share of Portland cement and the dosage fall, the crystallisation may slow down ({CL210})
CA_STEPS|/waterA/title: Choose the product for drinking water
CA_STEPS|/waterA/short: {CL170}, {CP360} and {CP350} are tested after DVGW W 270 and W 347; {CL210} is used where drinking water is not involved.
CA_STEPS|/waterA/overview: For tanks and structures in contact with drinking water the admixture must be suitable for it: {CL170}, {CP360} and {CP350} are tested after the DVGW worksheets W 270 (microbiological) and W 347 (hygienic) and suitable for drinking water. {CL210} is not tested for drinking water and is used for the other water-retaining and ground-contact structures.
CA_STEPS|/waterA/points/0: the test reports after W 270 and W 347 are available for download with the product
CA_STEPS|/waterA/points/1: no lining to taint the water, lift or age: the crystals are part of the concrete
CA_STEPS|/waterA/points/2: the filled tank is vapour permeable to the outside and watertight to the inside
CA_STEPS|/saltA/short: Reduced chloride ion migration, lower carbonation speed, improved freeze–thaw resistance; {CL210} is most effective in exposure class XS.
CA_STEPS|/saltA/overview: Components exposed to frost, de-icing salt or sea water need a concrete that keeps the chlorides away from the reinforcement: BETOCRETE reduces the chloride ion migration and improves the frost and freeze–thaw resistance; {CL210} and {CP360} also lower the carbonation speed. {CL210} shows the highest effectiveness in exposure class XS. The test reports of {CL210} cover freeze–thaw–salt resistance, chloride migration, carbonation and the depth of water penetration under pressure.
CA_STEPS|/saltA/points/0: the German Federal Institute for Hydraulic Engineering (BAW) derives the service life from the chloride migration coefficient and the concrete cover: a test report shows a 2.5-fold service life for a BETOCRETE concrete against the reference
CA_STEPS|/saltA/points/1: {CP350} adds a corrosion inhibitor where the steel is at risk
CA_STEPS|/saltA/points/2: exposure class XA3 (chemical attack) is excluded for all four products
CAS_T|/cabase/name: Base slab and walls below ground
CAS_T|/cabase/problem: A basement stands in the ground: soil moisture and ground water press against the slab and the walls, the construction joint at the kicker is the weak point, and the cracks that every slab and wall develop would carry the water inside. An external membrane needs a weather window, protection boards and an excavation for every repair.
CAS_T|/cabase/solution: Slab and walls are cast in watertight concrete with BETOCRETE — {CL170} or {CL210} dosed with the mixing water at the plant, {CP360} as water-soluble bags where the truck is dosed on site. The crystalline waterstop {CJ5} stands in the kicker, the swelling tape {CJ6} on working joints, the injection hose {CJ1} as reserve. When the ground water rises the pores close; cracks up to 0.4 mm heal themselves; the inside stays dry and vapour permeable. Technical drawings TD 5.10.01a and 5.10.01b.
CAS_T|/capit/name: Lift pit below the ground water
CAS_T|/capit/problem: The pit of a lift shaft is the deepest point of the building, below the ground water table on all sides, reachable only from the inside: slab, walls and kicker joint carry pressing water from the first day, and the buffers, rails and anchors must be fixed to dry concrete.
CAS_T|/capit/solution: The pit is cast in BETOCRETE concrete — {CP360} or {CP350} as 3 kg water-soluble bags into the drum of the mixer truck on site, approx. 1 minute of mixing per m³ and at least 5 minutes — with the crystalline waterstop {CJ5} in the kicker and the injection hose {CJ1} as reserve where the pit cannot be reached later. Crack-width limits by the structural engineer; component thickness ≥ 15 cm. The pit stays dry; a crack from settlement or shrinkage closes itself. Technical drawing TD 5.10.02.
CAS_T|/catank/problem: A tank holds water permanently from the inside: joints between slab and wall, inlets and the fine cracks of a filled tank would leak, and a lining could taint the water, lift or age. For drinking water the admixture itself must be suitable.
